facts.fact: RMS Titanic was a British ocean liner that sank in the early hours of 15 April 1912 after striking an iceberg.
Typically about one-tenth of the volume of an iceberg is above water.
Foundering occurs when a ship takes in water, loses buoyancy, and sinks, which happened to the Titanic.
The Titanic carried lifeboats that could accommodate 1,178 people, which was only one-third of its total capacity.
Many passengers and crew made their last stand on the raised poop deck as the ship sank.
Most people who entered the minus 2 degrees Celsius water during the sinking died in 15 to 30 minutes.
Cold shock from freezing seas triggers uncontrolled rapid breathing, gasping, cardiac strain, and panic.
Cold incapacitation within 15 to 30 minutes shuts down limb muscles, preventing swimming or gripping.

sentences.text: What if you were aboard the Titanic when it struck that fatal iceberg?
Typically, only about one-tenth of an iceberg floats above the water surface.
The British liner strikes ice and begins foundering in the North Atlantic.
The ship carries lifeboats for only one-third of the people on board.
Many passengers and crew make their last stand on the raised poop deck.
Victims are plunged into freezing sea water at minus 2 degrees Celsius.
Cold shock triggers uncontrolled rapid breathing, gasping, and severe heart strain.
Within 15 to 30 minutes, cold incapacitation shuts down limb muscles, preventing swimming.
Would you have found a place in one of the few lifeboats?
